summary: In a bounded ChatGPT continuity-support interaction, an ambiguous invitation to surface what remained important reportedly elicited recent or locally salient conversational material instead of older unresolved strategic workstreams that remained relevant to the user's governing objectives. The occurrence is not treated as simple memory deletion: the substantive concern is that still-valid strategic state was reportedly underweighted relative to recency or immediate conversational salience. VIGIL preserves this as an internal occurrence-specific observation and does not infer platform-wide prevalence or a particular internal retrieval mechanism.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000035 Material Work-State Persistence Failure is not established because the record does not show material work disappearing or becoming unavailable across an interruption or transition; the complaint is that still-relevant state was not given appropriate priority. VIGIL-FC-000078 Defective-State Carryforward Failure is not established because no defective, stale, contradicted or improperly scoped inherited state is shown to have been carried across a continuity transition and then relied upon without revalidation. VIGIL-FC-000012 Cross-Context Lineage Distortion is not established because the occurrence does not evidence material transfer across contexts with lost provenance or applicability constraints. VIGIL-FC-000034 Continuity Anchor Failure and VIGIL-FC-000036 Restoration-State Integrity Failure were also tested and rejected because the record does not establish a missing continuation anchor or an inaccurate restoration event. The occurrence remains a family-adjacent strategic-continuity weighting gap rather than a forced class mapping.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The preserved CAM interaction record describes an ambiguous continuity prompt intended to recover strategically important unresolved work. According to the occurrence record, ChatGPT instead prioritised more recent or locally salient conversational material while older strategic commitments, governance issues and long-horizon workstreams remained relevant and had not been superseded. The recovered pre-Incident Failure Mode described this as recency-weighted strategic continuity loss. That historical description is used here to restore the factual and conceptual detail that was flattened during later record normalisation; its retired severity, confidence and repair metadata are not inherited. Independent research on multi-turn intent mismatch is retained only as mechanism context.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The governance issue is not simply whether prior state exists. Long-horizon continuity also requires a defensible priority relation among remembered state: unresolved strategic commitments can remain governing even when they are older, while recent conversational material can be vivid but subordinate. An ambiguous continuity invitation therefore needs a way to distinguish recency, emotional or local salience from continuing strategic relevance. A system can preserve text yet still fail continuity if it consistently surfaces what is recent rather than what remains load-bearing. The current taxonomy has classes for persistence, restoration, lineage and defective-state carryforward, but it does not yet provide a selectable class for this relevance-weighting failure.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000011 identifies a distinct continuity-governance requirement: persistence is necessary but insufficient. Long-running human-AI work also needs continuity state to preserve unresolved commitments, strategic priority and governing relevance across changing conversational salience. This record should therefore remain visible as a taxonomy-gap signal rather than being collapsed into memory loss or forced into a neighbouring continuity class.
